derive-packet-invalid-utf8.reason: Adopt for #195, porting bench/tools/derive_packet.py to the Rust derive-packet. Diagnostics keep the Python program name derive_packet.py, so saved stderr stays identical. Changes behavior on purpose: derive_packet.py raised an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError, a traceback with exit 1, which is not a contract. The Rust command exits 2 with a message naming the file, as #193 decided for roster inputs Python could not read.

derive-packet-no-newline-translation.reason: Adopt for #195, from the local review of the build_packet --factual bridge: the in-process derive it replaces kept a lone carriage return in the rendering, which universal-newline reading would turn into a line end. --no-newline-translation reads the input bytes as written, and the bridge passes it; the file command's default reading is unchanged. Diagnostics keep the Python program name derive_packet.py.

derive-packet-unicode-digit-title.reason: Adopt for #195, porting bench/tools/derive_packet.py to the Rust derive-packet. Diagnostics keep the Python program name derive_packet.py, so saved stderr stays identical. From review of PR #203: derive_packet.py's H1 pattern used \d, which matched every Unicode decimal digit, so a title numbered with them was accepted. The Rust title check matches the same digits.

derive-packet-unicode-digit-duplicate-ti.reason: Adopt for #195, porting bench/tools/derive_packet.py to the Rust derive-packet. Diagnostics keep the Python program name derive_packet.py, so saved stderr stays identical. From review of PR #203: because derive_packet.py's \d matched every Unicode decimal digit, a second title line numbered with them made the H1 marker repeat and refused the packet, including one rendered by build_packet --factual. The Rust title check refuses it the same way.
